headline: The Eastern Province is building commercial floorspace faster than its usual pattern
deck: Three awards in Al Khobar within weeks describe a conurbation whose development has historically followed industrial employment rather than leading it.
excerpt: Saudi Downtown Company's infrastructure package, Retal's SAR 268m business court and Kortech's entertainment complex services scope all landed in Al Khobar within weeks of each other, which is not the usual rhythm for the Eastern Province.
content:
Three contract awards in Al Khobar within a few weeks are worth reading together, because the Eastern Province does not usually generate that concentration of commercial development.

Saudi Downtown Company, a Public Investment Fund unit, awarded Ansab the design and infrastructure development works at its Al Khobar Downtown project, a mixed-use site of approximately 829,103 square metres. Retal Urban Development's subsidiary signed a SAR 267.98m design and building services contract for the Remal Business Court. And Hassan Allam Holding's subsidiary Kortech took the mechanical, electrical and plumbing scope at Saudi Entertainment Ventures' Al Khobar Entertainment Complex.

Infrastructure, offices and leisure, in the same city, in the same window.

The Eastern Province has a development history unlike Riyadh's or the Red Sea coast's. Dammam, Dhahran and Al Khobar grew around the oil industry, and their built environment followed industrial employment: housing for workers, services for those households, and commercial space in proportion to a population whose primary economic activity was elsewhere on the map, at Jubail, Ras Tanura and Abqaiq.

That produces a particular pattern. Development tends to be incremental, demand-led and privately financed, rather than the programme-led development seen where a masterplanned district is delivered as a single act of policy.

What these three awards describe is closer to the second model. A Public Investment Fund vehicle procuring enabling infrastructure across an 829,000 square metre site is programme-led development, and it is aimed at creating urban destination rather than responding to existing demand.

Saudi Entertainment Ventures' presence points the same way. An entertainment complex combining an aquarium, cinema, family entertainment centre, black box venue and observation wheel is a leisure destination sized for a regional catchment rather than a neighbourhood.

The commercial logic is population and income. The Eastern Province conurbation is large, its household incomes are among the Kingdom's higher ones, and its discretionary spending has historically leaked to Bahrain and to Riyadh for the categories that were not available locally. Building those categories locally captures the spend.

For contractors the interest is in the mix. Infrastructure packages are accessible to a broad population of Saudi firms. Business court structures and services are mid-market building work. An entertainment complex with an aquarium and an observation wheel is specialist services work with an integrated commissioning problem, which is a much narrower field.

Read against a national construction market of roughly $142.30bn growing near 3.6 per cent in real terms, three awards do not make a boom. They do mark a change in what the Eastern Province is building and who is paying for it.
author: BrentDesk Staff
seoTitle: Al Khobar is building commercial floorspace unusually fast
